text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a project all at once, teams use an iterative process. They break the work into small, manageable phases called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. At the start of each sprint, the team reviews its backlog, which is a prioritized list of tasks. These tasks are often written as user stories, short descriptions of features from the user’s perspective. Every day, the team holds a quick standup meeting, where each member shares what they did yesterday and what they plan to do today. This keeps everyone aligned and allows them to adapt quickly to any changes, ensuring that the final product truly meets the customer's needs.
